name: Net-Kill Lunge
execution: Deficit Front-Foot Elevated DB Lunge + Backward Hop
swap: Forward Lunge + Push Back

name: Jump Smash Landing
execution: Trap Bar Jump (Bilateral Landing) + Unweighted Drop-Lunge Stick
swap: DB Jump Squat + Split Landing

name: Smash Pronation
execution: Triceps Pull + Rear Delt Raise
swap: Band Pushdown + Reverse Fly

name: Low Defensive Dig
execution: Cossack Squat + Lateral Bound
swap: Lateral Lunge + Skater Jump

name: Extreme Lunge & Rebound
execution: Heavy Front-Foot Elevated DB Lunge (Drop Weights at bottom) + Bodyweight Explosive Backward Push-Off
swap: DB Deficit Lunge to fast backpedal

manual.why: Badminton requires lunging at angles exceeding 100 degrees of knee flexion.
manual.cue: We're building the brakes and the springs in your knees.

name: Scissor-Kick Vertical Brake
execution: Submaximal Trap Bar Jump + immediate single-leg landing with a 2-second isometric stick.
swap: DB Jump Squat to single-leg stick

manual.why: The jump smash requires massive vertical thrust, but the landing is single-leg.
manual.cue: You can jump as high as you want, but if your knee caves in on landing, you'll get hurt.

name: Terminal Pronation & Cuff Brake
focus: Forearm Pronation Velocity & Posterior Cuff Eccentrics
execution: High-cable triceps pull-down with aggressive forearm pronation + Prone DB Trap-3 raise (slow eccentric).
swap: Resistance band overhead snap + Band pull-aparts

manual.why: The badminton smash relies heavily on violent forearm pronation.
manual.cue: To hit a heavy smash, your forearm has to snap like a whip, and we build the brakes too.

name: Net Low-Lunge Brace Hold
execution: Front-Foot Elevated DB Split Squat to badminton depth, moderate load, 4 reps/side + Immediate 3s bottom-position isometric brace with the DBs at the shoulders while a partner pushes down on the front thigh
swap: Bodyweight front-foot elevated split squat to a 3s bottom brace hold, no partner needed

manual.why: Supersedes id 21, which duplicated id 48 and chained a backward hop onto dumbbells with no stated release. This version keeps the net-depth demand but drops the plyometric, so there is no load-exit problem, and it leans on the isometric hold instead of the rebound, which is what actually breaks down in a long low rally.
manual.cue: Sink to the net, then prove you can hold it while someone tries to push you over.

name: Jump Smash Two-Foot Rebound
execution: Submaximal Trap Bar Jump, 20-30% max, 5 reps, two-foot landing with a 2s hold + Immediate bodyweight two-foot re-drive jump off the same landing, 5 reps
swap: Light DB jump squat + immediate bodyweight re-drive jump, both feet

manual.why: Supersedes id 22, which duplicated id 49 and put a loaded trap bar jump straight into a single-leg landing stick. This version stays two-foot throughout so the unilateral landing work lives in one place (id 49), and the trap bar is only ever landed from off both feet.
manual.cue: Land quiet on both feet, then spring back up before the second foot has settled.

name: Smash Arm-Speed Snap
focus: Low-Load Elbow Extension Velocity and Wrist Snap
execution: Light DB triceps kickback, 20-30% max, elbow pinned high, 6 reps/side + Immediate band wrist-extension snap, fast, 6 reps/side
swap: Band triceps pushdown + band wrist-extension snap

manual.why: Supersedes id 23, whose execution contained no forearm rotation at all, so it did not match the force vector it was named for, and it reversed direction mid-complex by going from a triceps pull to a rear delt raise. This version is the fast low-load accelerator; id 50 keeps the heavy pronation and the slow cuff eccentrics as the brakes.
manual.cue: Light and fast, elbow locked high, snap the wrist over the last inch.

name: Feint-Read First Step
focus: Reactive First-Step Launch off an Unpredictable Cue
execution: Split-step, hold 2s on partner's call, then fire the first step to the direction the partner calls out, 6 reps/side + Immediate lateral push-off back to base and re-set the split-step
swap: Same drill with a single partner calling the direction from behind the athlete, so no visual target placement is needed at all

manual.why: Badminton had no reactive complex at all, and reacting to the opponent's contact is the most specific thing a badminton player does. Cricket and tennis each have two; this fills the badminton gap rather than duplicating them because the target distance is shuttle-court length and the recovery is the split-step re-set.
manual.cue: Your opponent is lying to you. Read the body, not the racket.

name: Rear-Court Whip Turn
focus: 180-Degree Rear-to-Front Rotation from a Low Split Base
execution: Band-resisted 180-degree split turn, rear-to-front, 4 reps/side + Immediate med ball rotational chest pass to the wall, 4 reps/side
swap: Bodyweight 180-degree split turn + med ball chest pass to a partner

manual.why: Badminton had no rotational complex, yet the rear-court to front-court turn is the most shuttle-specific pattern in the sport. It is built from a low split base because that is where the turn actually has to happen, not from a tall athletic stance.
manual.cue: Turn low, finish facing the net, throw before you have finished standing up.

name: Deep-Lunge Hamstring Eccentric
focus: Hamstring Eccentric Length at Maximum Lunge Depth
execution: Front-foot elevated DB split squat onto a slider, 4s eccentric to full badminton depth, 3 reps/side with the DBs at the shoulders + Immediate bodyweight slider hamstring curl to full stand
swap: Bodyweight 4s eccentric split squat with the front heel on a bench + bodyweight slider curl

manual.why: Badminton lunges go deeper than any other court in this database and the hamstring is the limiter at full knee flexion, but every existing badminton complex is knee-dominant. Cricket has both the eccentric and the slider work; badminton had neither.
manual.cue: Sit down into the bottom, do not bail out of it, then stand up with the heel dug in.

name: Rear-Court Whip Turn
focus: 180-Degree Rear-to-Front Rotation from a Low Split Base
execution: Band-resisted 180-degree split turn, rear-to-front, 4 reps/side + Immediate med ball rotational chest pass to the wall, 4 reps/side
swap: Bodyweight 180-degree split turn + med ball chest pass to a partner

manual.why: Supersedes id 97 for one reason only: to drop an unused 'Cones' tag from equipment. The execution and swap never mentioned cones, so the tag was inaccurate and would send a coach hunting for equipment the drill does not need. No change to focus, execution, swap, category, role, or also_suits. The rotation itself is unchanged and still the badminton gap-fill it was proposed as — badminton still had no rotational complex.
manual.cue: Turn low, finish facing the net, throw before you have finished standing up.

goals: turning quickly from back to front court
